translation_notes: the stratum's own construction: `OCHRE = Namespace(settings.OCHRE_NAMESPACE)` is declared inside the function, bound to a value computed at run time (Django settings), not a string literal. Translated to `@prefix ochre: f<{settings.OCHRE_NAMESPACE}> .` -- the dynamic-@prefix form in declarations.md (`@prefix dyn: f<http://{host}/ns#> .`), block-scoped to the function.

the source also has a second, dead local `ns = Namespace(settings.OCHRE_NAMESPACE)` (never read afterwards). Translated it too, as `@prefix ns: f<{settings.OCHRE_NAMESPACE}> .`, unused in exactly the same way -- not mine to drop under the no-refactoring rule.

`OCHRE["equivalentClass"]` etc. (subscript access on the Namespace) became `ochre:equivalentClass` etc., used as plain Python list elements inside `if p in [...]` -- a prefixed name is an ordinary URIRef-valued expression, no island needed there.

`for s, p, o in g:` with a Python-side filter is a full, unfiltered graph traversal (`what-not-to-rewrite` in migrate-from-rdflib.md): kept as plain rdflib iteration, not forced into `m{ }`, which is reserved for a pattern that actually selects.
`g.add((k, RDFS["comment"], v))` -> `+{ {k} rdfs:comment {v} }` under `@graph g` (designating the existing variable, not creating a new one).
